paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the overall analysis pipeline as three consecutive stages (data generation → vulnerability-index (VI) definition & selection → surrogate-based global sensitivity analysis).
must_not_claim: any simulation results or sensitivity outcomes
that a particular VI is superior (selection/results belong in Results)

paragraphs.purpose: Describe the computational data-generation step: the cost-effective pulsatile fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations used to produce the dataset, and reference boundary-condition and waveform inputs.
must_not_claim: any performance claims about the FSI method beyond citing prior validation (do not claim new validation here)
simulation outcomes or sensitivity results

paragraphs.purpose: Specify the two plaque phenotype models (LAP: 3-domain, CP: 4-domain) and modeling assumptions including the uniform fibrous cap (FC) thickness treated as a single scalar parameter.
must_not_claim: that these two phenotypes exhaust clinical variability
any findings about which phenotype yields higher risk

paragraphs.purpose: Define the input design space: three parameter groups (morphology, hemodynamics, material) and the 1,000-sample experimental design used to span that space.
must_not_claim: results of sensitivity analysis or dominance of any group

paragraphs.purpose: State the simulation outputs recorded for each sample: PSS (peak stress), ΔPSS (stress amplitude; spherical mean), and a rupture-location index.
must_not_claim: that these outputs already demonstrate predictive superiority (interpretation reserved for Results/Discussion)

paragraphs.purpose: Define the vulnerability-index (VI) candidates: stress/strength formulation with two stress measures (PSS, ΔPSS) and three strength scenarios (yielding 2×3=6 candidates); provide their formulaic expressions and indicate the candidate table.
must_not_claim: that any candidate is preferred (selection is in a later paragraph/Results)
results of validation or clinical performance

paragraphs.purpose: Describe the VI selection procedure: use of seven clinically established high-risk plaque sign criteria (sign/anti-sign matching) to screen the six candidates and select the final VIs (VI1=ΔPSS/E_FC^0.5, VI2=ΔPSS/E_FC^1.0); reference the selection table.
must_not_claim: quantitative superiority beyond the stated selection rule (statistical performance is in Results)
that the selected VIs are universally optimal for all clinical scenarios

paragraphs.purpose: Explain surrogate modeling and global sensitivity analysis: training Gaussian-process regressors on the final VI outputs (report LAP 784 / CP 727 effective pairs), describe that the surrogate enables ≈1.5×10^4 inexpensive evaluations, and state that Sobol first-order and total-order indices were computed on the surrogate for group- and parameter-level sensitivity.
must_not_claim: interpretations of sensitivity results (those belong in Results/Discussion)
that the surrogate replaces the need for any FSI validation (surrogate is an emulator for GSA purposes only)

paragraphs.purpose: Establish that the simulation outputs (PSS, FFR, rupture-location trends) are consistent with prior literature, thereby validating the cost‑effective pulsatile FSI pipeline used to generate the dataset.
must_not_claim: Do not claim perfect patient-specific fidelity or clinical outcome prediction from these simulations.
Do not claim novelty or validation of the cost‑effective FSI method itself (method is out of scope).
Do not assert causal clinical conclusions based solely on simulation agreement.

paragraphs.purpose: Report the set of six candidate vulnerability indices (2 stress × 3 strength scenarios), show the selection procedure against seven established clinical high‑risk plaque signs, and state that two indices (VI1, VI2) were chosen.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the selected VIs have been prospectively clinically validated beyond the sign‑matching selection criterion.
Do not present method details that belong in Methods (keep to results of the selection).
Do not claim that alternative selection rules would not be reasonable.

paragraphs.purpose: Present the global sensitivity analysis results (group‑level and parameter‑level Sobol indices) that show material properties dominate variance in the selected VIs and identify the top individual drivers (E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP).
must_not_claim: Do not overinterpret Sobol indices as proof of causality in patients; they quantify contributions to output variance within the modeled design space and chosen VI definitions only.
Do not claim the identified ranking necessarily generalizes outside the sampled input ranges or alternative VI formulations without further study.
Do not provide clinical recommendations or policy implications here (leave to Discussion).

paragraphs.purpose: State and justify the finding that ΔPSS (stress amplitude, fatigue viewpoint) is a stronger predictor of plaque rupture vulnerability than peak PSS, and motivate the need for pulsatile (FSI) analyses.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical causality or proven predictive value in patient populations beyond model-based evidence
Do not claim that peak PSS has no relevance in all contexts

paragraphs.purpose: Discuss why vulnerability indices must be normalized by material strength (stress/strength), explain that the normalization exponent α matters, and link this to how the six candidate VIs were constructed and screened.
must_not_claim: Do not claim a single universally optimal α (exponent) valid for all patients
Do not assert that strength normalization fully resolves all patient-level uncertainty

paragraphs.purpose: Interpret the global sensitivity results: show that material properties dominate over hemodynamic and morphological factors (Material > Hemo > Morpho), identify the top individual drivers, and draw implications for clinical risk-stratification priorities.
must_not_claim: Do not claim immediate clinical guidelines or specify new diagnostic thresholds solely from these model-based sensitivity rankings
Do not claim morphology measurements are uninformative in all cases

paragraphs.purpose: Enumerate study limitations and scope: model idealizations, assumptions (uniform fibrous cap thickness, ideal arterial geometry), surrogate approximation, and clarify that cost-effective FSI algorithm validation is out of scope (cited literature covers that).
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the cost-effective FSI method is newly validated here or that it outperforms other FSI techniques (this is out_of_scope)
Do not claim generalizability to all patient anatomies without additional validation

paragraphs.purpose: State the clinical importance: coronary plaque rupture is the principal cause of acute coronary syndromes and contributes substantially to cardiovascular mortality, motivating quantitative rupture-risk assessment.
must_not_claim: method details (e.g., describe our simulations or dataset)
study results or conclusions about which factors dominate

paragraphs.purpose: Explain that rupture vulnerability is determined by interacting morphological, hemodynamic, and material (strength) factors—establishing the multi-factor nature of the problem to be analyzed.
must_not_claim: that any single factor is already proven dominant
methodological specifics of how to quantify each factor

paragraphs.purpose: Identify the gap: prior computational vulnerability indices commonly use stress-only metrics and ignore patient-specific strength; argue on structural-mechanics grounds that a stress/strength ratio is the appropriate physical frame to account for strength uncertainty.
must_not_claim: that existing stress-only studies are unusable in all clinical contexts
specific numerical results (these belong in Methods/Results)

paragraphs.purpose: Motivate the need for a global sensitivity analysis that varies morphology, hemodynamics, and material properties simultaneously over a realistic vulnerability-index (VI) space to determine which factor-group should be prioritized clinically; note that high computational cost has prevented such comprehensive analyses to date.
must_not_claim: description of the specific computational technique used in this paper (save for the Methods)
any results about which group is dominant

paragraphs.purpose: State this study's aim and scope: using a previously validated, cost‑efficient pulsatile FSI pipeline to generate large datasets across realistic input-space (including strength) and to perform surrogate‑based Sobol global sensitivity analysis testing ΔPSS‑based stress/strength VIs to assess clinical plausibility and identify dominant determinants.
must_not_claim: presenting results (e.g., that ΔPSS is superior or that material properties dominate) — results must be reported in the Results section
claiming to introduce a new FSI algorithm (the cost-effective FSI is adopted from prior validated work)

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the study's primary quantitative findings (ΔPSS-based VI selection and dominance of material properties and blood pressure in driving rupture vulnerability).
must_not_claim: must_not_claim that these model results constitute direct patient-level clinical prediction
must_not_claim causal mechanisms in vivo beyond the scope of the simulations
must_not claim the FSI implementation itself as a novel methodological contribution

paragraphs.purpose: State the practical implication for prioritizing measurement/stratification efforts (material-property characterization should be emphasized if material dominance holds).
must_not_claim: must_not_claim that the study proves material measurement will definitively improve clinical outcomes
must_not_claim that morphology-based imaging is unimportant in all cases

paragraphs.purpose: Conclude methodological implications: ΔPSS (stress amplitude) is a more clinically appropriate stress metric and vulnerability indices must normalize by strength (α matters); therefore pulsatile (fatigue-capable) analyses and careful strength-normalization are warranted in future work.
must_not_claim: must_not_claim that the cost-effective FSI approach introduced here is being proposed as a novel validated solver (out_of_scope)
must_not claim that a single choice of α is universally correct without further validation

paragraphs.purpose: Highlight limitations and concrete next steps: sensitivity to the strength-normalization exponent α, need for patient-specific material characterization and clinical validation of the proposed VIs.
must_not_claim: must_not_claim that clinical validation has been performed
must_not claim that the identified VIs are ready for clinical deployment without prospective testing

paragraphs.purpose: State clinical importance of coronary plaque rupture and motivate need for better rupture-risk metrics.
must_not_claim: presenting any new clinical trial or epidemiologic analysis
providing quantitative results from this study

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the mechanistic determinants of rupture (morphology, hemodynamics, material strength) and structural-mechanics rationale for stress/strength framing.
must_not_claim: quantitatively ranking determinants (defer to Results)
that any single prior study fully resolved the multi-factor interaction

paragraphs.purpose: Identify the methodological gap: prior computational risk indices commonly use stress-only metrics and ignore patient-specific strength uncertainty, motivating a normalized stress/strength vulnerability index.
must_not_claim: that every prior paper ignored strength in all modelling contexts (avoid overgeneralization)

paragraphs.purpose: State the need for a global sensitivity analysis across morphology/hemodynamics/materials over a realistic vulnerability-index (VI) space and note prior computational cost barriers.
must_not_claim: that no previous study has attempted any sensitivity analysis in any simplified setting (avoid absolute negation)

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize this study's approach (cost-effective pulsatile FSI data generation, VI candidate definition and selection, GPR surrogate + Sobol global sensitivity) and state the main quantitative findings and implications (ΔPSS-based VI preferred; strength-normalized VI; material properties and SBP/PP dominate).
must_not_claim: that the cost-effective FSI algorithm itself is a novel methodological contribution (out of scope)
causal clinical recommendations beyond the study's sensitivity/association findings
that the selected VI(s) are validated in prospective clinical outcome cohorts
